16.06.2023 Heard Mr. U.K. Nair, learned senior counsel assisted by Mr. K. Kalita, learned counsel for the petitioner as well as Ms. G. Hazarika, learned standing counsel for the Revenue Department appearing for the respondent nos.1, 2 and 3 and Mr. CKS Baruah, learned Govt. Advocate appearing for the respondent no.4, and Ms. G. Goswami, learned counsel for the respondent no.5/ Caveator.
2.
By filing this writ petition under Article 226 of the Constitution of India, the petitioner has assailed the order dated 13.03.2023 issued by the Deputy Commissioner, Tinsukia.

It appears that the said order was passed pursuant to order dated 02.03.2023 passed in WP(C) 7797/2017 and in WP(C) 6290/2017.
3.

The Deputy Commissioner, Tinsukia by the said impugned order had held that the proceedings of LA case no.192/2011 and LA case no.193/2011 are not disposed and that payment as ordered by the Deputy Commissioner, Tinsukia was not deposited in the account of the land owners.

Accordingly, it was held that the land acquisition proceedings is deemed to have lapsed as per Page No.# 3/5 section 24 of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 and it was observed that no awards were passed in the said two LA cases as per section 11 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1984 and accordingly, it was held that the determination of compensation would be in accordance with the 2013 Act.
4. Issue notice of motion returnable in 4(four) weeks.
5. Requisite extra copies of the writ petition be served on the learned State and Departmental counsel in course of the day within 2(two) days.
6. Heard both sides on the prayer for interim relief.
7. It prima facie appears that the possession of the land was initially taken over in terms of Rule 189 and 190 of the Rules under the Assam Land and Revenue Regulation, 1886 under a prospecting Oil India Ltd vs The State Of Assam And 4 Ors on 16 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/112507084/
2 license.

sentences.text: An effort to determine the compensation proceedings, quantum of compensation was negotiated between the parties but as zonal land valuation was not decided, the parties had agreed that the final compensation would be dependent on the zonal valuation which would be given retrospective effect.
8. It also appears that subsequently the land acquisition proceedings were initiated by issuing a land acquisition notification on 20.05.2011, under section 4 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894.

While the learned senior counsel for the petitioner submits that an award was passed, the same is disputed by Ms. G. Goswami, learned counsel appearing for the respondent no.5 by submitting that the quantum of compensation which was determined was a continuation of the compensation which was to be granted for mining lease which does not constitute the award under the Land Acquisition Act, 1894.

10. She has also submitted that pursuant to the Constitution bench Judgment of the Supreme Court of India in the case of Indore Development Authority Vs. Manohar Lal, 2020 8 SCC 129, her case is that now the quantum of compensation ought to be calculated under the 2013 Act.

entities.text: Indore Development Authority Vs. Manohar Lal, 2020 8 SCC 129
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 11. Be that as it may in this case we find that the quantum of compensation as was determined by the Deputy Commissioner, Tinsukia as per the letter dated 27.05.2023 is Rs.22,21,72,794/-.

Moreover,
considering that the original award was for an amount of Rs.6,30,21,217/- and on addition of quantum of interest and solatium may exceed twice the amount of the award, the Court is of the considered opinion that as an interim measure, the petitioner be directed to deposit a sum of Rs.
9.00 crore in addition to whatever amount that has already been deposited, which shall be done within a period of one month from today and on such deposit being made, the quantum of compensation demanded by letter dated 27.05.2023 by the Collector-cum- Deputy Commissioner,
Tinsukia shall not be enforced till the next date of listing.

12. In the event, the Collector-cum-Deputy Commissioner, Tinsukia does not file an affidavit in the matter, he would produce the records relating to LA Page No.# 5/5 case no.192/2011 and 193/2011 as well as true copy of the award register, if maintained separately, including the order of approval,
if any, issued by the competent authority in the Govt. of Assam.
